On January 1st, several significant events occurred in the Roman Empire. The Julian calendar took effect as the civil calendar of the Roman Empire, establishing January 1st as the new date of the new year. In the year 366, the Alemanni invaded the Roman Empire by crossing the frozen Rhine in large numbers. In 250, Emperor Decius ordered everyone in the Roman Empire (except Jews) to make sacrifices to the Roman gods. On January 16th, in the year -27, Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus was granted the title Augustus by the Roman Senate, marking the beginning of the Roman Empire. On January 19th, in the year 379, Emperor Gratian elevated Flavius Theodosius at Sirmium to Augustus and gave him authority over all the eastern provinces of the Roman Empire.
